---
title: Global audit of collision of the scores
---
These go scripts verify that the fundamental building blocks are independent given a specific set of delta values. 
They simulate all 100 possible position-delta combinations and check for any shared square-free cores, which would indicate potential structural dependencies under Besicovitch's Theorem. 

# structural dependencies in 1D
```{sh}
#golang_1.24.5
go mod init global_audit
go mod tidy
go run audit_collision_1D.go  
```
Analysis of all possible position-delta combinations ...

⚠️ Audit failed: Found 7 potential structural dependencies.

Square-Free Core   Combination A             Combination B            
102                Pos 1 with delta=0.02         Pos 4 with delta=0.08        
3                  Pos 1 with delta=0.08         Pos 5 with delta=0.07        
78                 Pos 3 with delta=0.12         Pos 7 with delta=0.02        
202                Pos 2 with delta=0.02         Pos 8 with delta=0.08

57                 Pos 5 with delta=0.13         Pos 9 with delta=0.12        
7                  Pos 1 with delta=0.12         Pos 10 with delta=0.08       

Insight: Because these combinations share a base, specific cross-position mutations could mimic each other.


# Higher-Dimensional Audit (audit_collision_2D.go)
The script simulates two different reference coordinate systems to see if those 7 collisions vanish in 2D space.
To audit the 2D projection system, each position-delta combination is evaluated using two separate reference metrics (RX and RY).
1.	We compute the square-free cores for Axis X.
2.	We compute the square-free cores for Axis Y.
3.	We merge them into a coordinate core pair: (CoreX, CoreY).
4.	We check if this exact ordered pair repeats anywhere else in the matrix.

More specifically, the first axis represents our standard base configuration. It calculates the radicand directly from the natural left-to-right position of the sequence:
RadicandX = position + delta
The second axis simulates a secondary reference point by inverting the positional distance calculation:
RadicandY = (11 - position) + delta
For Position 1, Axis Y treats it as being a distance of 10 units away from the opposite end (11 - 1 = 10). For Position 9, it treats it as being 2 units away (11 - 9 = 2).
By pairing these two calculations, every position-delta combination receives a dual geometric identity: a coordinate pair of square-free cores (CoreX, CoreY).


```{sh}
go run audit_collision_2D.go  
```
✅ 2D geometric audit passed!

Result: Zero multi-dimensional coordinate collisions found.
Conclusion: While 1D vector projections contain 7 algebraic overlaps, mapping across orthogonal reference axes entirely disperses these dependencies into unique 2D coordinates.
